proposed_results: For every fixed d >= 2, C_d(n) = Theta_d(n^(d-1) (log n)^(d-1)).
reason_for_investigation: The new prescribed-size lemma would match Wagner's inspected upper order in every fixed dimension, including the original dimension-three target. Overall priority and independent proof review are unestablished.
proof_mechanism: Uniform primitive-window sieve; divide primitive planes by their bounded integer heights to count normal directions; realize each lexicographic prefix by positive weights; use two nonnegative lattice patches at levels h-1 and h+1 to prove prescribed-size injectivity; separate aspect tuples by observable axis extents.

finite_evidence.limitations: Finite evidence does not prove the density asymptotics, the full argument or novelty.

checked_steps: Conditioning uses the joint projected events and preserves all next-step free coordinates.
The controlling determinant is nonzero for every allowed projected configuration.
Primitive projected rank at every prime gives exactly one bad residue for the last coordinate.
Large bad primes divide one fixed nonzero determinant; no infinite-union density interchange.
The all-dimensional closed threshold follows from elementary monotone exponential inequalities.
A primitive frame is the full parallel integer-lattice basis; scaled inverse bounds give injectivity.
Interior-vertex/chamber inequality holds for arbitrary degeneracies in an open convex domain.
Observable axis extents prevent duplicate cuts across scale tuples.
Explicit cardinality, composition, floor and constant calculations give the claimed uniform lower bound.
Lifting improves the exact-size lower exponent only in d>=4; the d=3 exact-size gap remains.

prime_base_realization.statement: Every nonempty finite corner cut is realizable as a smooth-number exponent prefix over distinct ordered prime bases, all above any prescribed bound B.
prime_base_realization.proof_location: paper/corner_cut_growth/main.tex, Proposition labelled prop:prime; docs/interleaving_research.md, Additional attribution and the exact prime-base connection
prime_base_realization.arithmetic_input: Classical Bertrand postulate; for sorted positive weights choose disjoint intervals (2^(i-1) exp(T w_i), 2^i exp(T w_i)).
prime_base_realization.source_inspected: Published text pp. 197--198, stating and completing the proof of Bertrand's postulate.
prime_base_realization.consequence: For every fixed B, S_{d,B}(n)=C_d(n), where S counts distinct prefix exponent sets over varying ordered tuples of distinct primes greater than B. Hence the cumulative theorem counts exactly the realizable smooth-prefix shapes.
prime_base_realization.scope: Elementary supporting proposition, no separate novelty claim. Varying prime tuples are essential; a single fixed tuple has only one prefix per length. No new prime-distribution or unranking claim.
